::: {.chapter-lead}
This page explains **how the components fit together** in an autoregressive Transformer. It is a high-level map; detailed definitions, derivations, and counterexamples live on dedicated pages.
:::

## What attention does

At each position, an autoregressive model must build a representation from the available prefix without consulting future tokens. Attention provides a learned way to weight information from other positions; causal masking enforces the ordering constraint.

![Original causal mask: each row can access its own and earlier positions.](images/causal-attention-mask.svg){fig-alt="Four-position matrix; current and earlier positions are visible while future positions are masked" width=100%}

## Concepts in computation order

1. **[Queries, keys, and values](queries-keys-values.qmd)** — three learned projections give representations distinct roles: searching, being matched, and providing aggregated information.
2. **[Scaled dot-product attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd)** — products (QK^\top) become scores; after scaling and softmax, they weight the values.
3. **[Causal masking](causal-masking.qmd)** — scores for future positions are excluded before softmax.
4. **[Mathematical foundations](mathematical-foundations.qmd)** — softmax reuses probability concepts; output logits then connect to likelihood and the training loss.
5. **[Cosine similarity](cosine-similarity.qmd)** — a useful comparison, but attention scores are not simply a universal measure of semantic similarity.

## Minimal mathematical view

For a sequence of length (T), let (X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d_{model}}) be the input representations. Learned projections produce (Q), (K), and (V). For one attention head:

[
\operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)
=\operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}+M\right)V.
]

Here, (M) is an additive mask: forbidden positions receive (-\infty). This formula combines several distinct choices; see the concept pages for dimensions, assumptions, and edge cases.

## Intuition, purpose, and limits

- **Intuition:** each position asks a question, compares accessible keys, and aggregates the corresponding values.
- **Purpose:** interactions between positions depend on learned content rather than a fixed local window in standard dense attention.
- **Limit:** attention alone is not a causal explanation of the model's decision or a guaranteed map of semantic importance.
- **Counterexample to an oversimplified intuition:** a high attention weight means a value contributes strongly to that aggregation, not that its source token must be the most important for the final prediction. Projections, residuals, other heads, and other layers also matter.

## Code and verification status

The repository does not yet contain a reusable attention module in `src/llm_lab/`. The small NumPy snippet in the previous version of this chapter was not a complete implementation: it only masked a score matrix. The priority is to validate the concepts and tests before adding the module.

- [Planned status and acceptance criteria for causal attention](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md#deferred--causal-attention-implementation)
- [Python implementation directory](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/tree/main/src/llm_lab)
- [Test directory](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/tree/main/tests)

A decisive test should check end-to-end causal invariance: changing a future token must not change outputs at earlier positions. Testing a mask matrix alone does not establish this property.
